title: Replica↔workflow equivalence is comment-enforced only — no durable pin on the 8-gate enumeration
evidence:
# The gate list mirrors .github/workflows/ci.yml step-for-step — the workflow
# is the spec; never edit one without the other. Same order, same failure
# semantics (stop on first failure), same per-gate names in the summary.
...
GATES=(
  "Purity + grep gates (ODN-1)|tools/lint.sh"
  "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|odin test core"
  "Game builds (app.bin compiles + links)|odin build app -out:app.bin"
  "Golden harness (T1 hashes + T2 software pixels + replay gate)|tools/harness.sh run"
  "W1 drift-rejection negative test|tools/harness.sh drift-check"
  "Assist preview cross-check (R2a preview == sim routing)|tools/harness.sh preview-check"
  "PP_DEBUG overlay builds (compile gate)|odin build app -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:app-debug.bin && odin build harness -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:bin/harness-debug"
  "Stats stream replay-identity (live == replay)|tools/harness.sh stats-check pause && tools/harness.sh stats-check qos_contention"
)
detail: The 8-gate list, order and commands are kept in sync with ci.yml only by a comment; a workflow edit silently orphans the replica. No existing test (lint, odin test, harness) executes or validates this tooling — regression would pass unnoticed.
recommended_fix: Add a --self-test mode (or small script) that greps ci.yml run steps and asserts they match the GATES labels/commands 1:1, order included; run it in --fast and document in README.

title: Stop-on-fail failure path never exercised — all verification claims are green runs
evidence:
if bash -c "$cmd"; then
      echo "   ✅ PASS"
      results+=("✅  gate $i  $label")
    else
      rc=$?
      echo "   ❌ FAIL (exit $rc)"
      results+=("❌  gate $i  $label")
      echo ""
      echo "gate $i failed — stopping (same failure semantics as CI)."
      break
    fi
detail: Every Verification claim is a green run; the ❌/skip/exit-1 stop-on-fail branch — the tool's one hard contract — has never been exercised, nor has the docker-build-failure path. Happy-path-only verification for a trust tool.
recommended_fix: Run the suite once with one deliberately broken gate (e.g. a temp failing lint) and capture the ❌ summary, ⏭ skip line and exit 1 in the spec's Verification section; or add a seeded-failure self-test.

title: windows-cross exit-0-with-warning semantics pinned by comments only; no test guards the missing-binary check
evidence:

  # for this platform is not yet supported" on stderr and exits 0 WITHOUT
  # emitting the binary — the exit code alone lies, so success = rc 0 AND the
  # artifact exists.
  local out rc
  rm -f app-win.exe
  out="$(odin build app -target:windows_amd64 -out:app-win.exe 2>&1)"
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -s app-win.exe ]; then
...
  echo "⚠️  windows-cross: failed as reported above — exiting 0 (experimental gate; see the PR for findings)."
  return 0
detail: Nothing but comments pins exit-0-with-warning: a future edit flipping the final return 0, or dropping the `-s app-win.exe` artifact check, passes silently. The check is correct today; no test would catch its removal.
recommended_fix: Add a stubbed-odin test of run_windows_cross: missing binary + rc 0 → warn + exit 0; present binary → success; non-zero rc → warn + exit 0. Wire into --self-test.
